prompts:
Use case: illustration-story. Transparent 6-frame sprite atlas (3 columns x2 rows) for the SAME cute Korean magpie.
Image1 is PRIMARY CHARACTER reference. Its TOP-LEFT bird is the EXACT final standing bird. Match that bird's plump belly, head outline, beak, long tail, white wing mark and thin belly border very closely. Image2 is only a MOTION reference: bottom row shows recovering from landing, raising the tail.
Draw six complete birds that bridge landing recovery to the PRIMARY standing pose, left to right then next row:
0 nearly folded wings, tail pointing right and only15 degrees upward; knees softly bent after landing, torso just a little lower than resting.
1 wings fully folded, tail23 degrees upward, legs beginning to straighten.
2 tail30 degrees upward, body gently rising.
3 tail36 degrees upward, legs almost at resting extension.
4 tail41 degrees upward, almost exactly primary resting bird.
5 exact primary reference TOP-LEFT standing bird, tail45 degrees upward.
CRITICAL: same bird, same head SIZE, same head shape, same round white eye and eye size, same beak, same body VOLUME, same tail LENGTH in all6. No zoom, inflated chest, thinner or taller replacement bird. Frame5 should be virtually identical to image1 top-left. Tiny natural leg/neck recovery only; do not split body into rigid puppet parts. Feet plant on the SAME baseline and in the SAME positions in each cell. Never float, hop, walk, or recenter on different feet. Charcoal #2e2a26 and white patches, clean silhouette, thin natural belly contour. Bodies face LEFT in all frames. Keep generous margins, no overlapping neighboring tails. Transparent background, no glow, shadows, floor, text, numbers or grid lines.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image1 is the EDIT TARGET: six landing-recovery magpie poses. Image2 is a CLOSE-UP of the CANONICAL HEAD AND BEAK that these birds MUST match. Image3 is the original full-character atlas, first bird is canonical standing. The current target heads have an angular triangular beak and sloping forehead; that is wrong. Correct the head/beak shapes in ALL SIX target birds to match the exact softer original profile shown in image2.
Copy the canonical beak contour: subtly rounded upper ridge where it joins forehead, longer low beak tip, gently curved underside; preserve the SAME beak length relative to head and same eye-to-tip distance as canonical. Copy the rounded forehead and crown from image2. These are not six different bird designs. Same exact side-facing head profile in every cell, at the existing head position and scale. Do not enlarge head. Keep small round white eye.
Preserve the six different tail angles and planted feet from image1. Keep body volume, folded wing pattern, thin belly outline, leg stance, grid positions and transparency unchanged. The final bottom-right bird should closely match the first bird in image3, including head-to-belly proportions and beak contour. This is an identity-continuity repair, not a new character. No shadow, glow, background, text, numbers or extra elements.

Edit ONLY the FIRST TWO birds in this six-pose magpie sheet. They are recovering from a landing:
Top-left bird should crouch slightly lower: lower its entire torso, head and wing by about12 pixels while keeping both toes planted at the same ground baseline. Bend its legs naturally to absorb this change. Keep body/head dimensions unchanged; this is posture, not smaller size.
Top-middle bird should be halfway recovered: lower torso, head and wing by about6 pixels, toes stay at same baseline; slightly bent legs.
Keep all other FOUR birds exactly unchanged. Keep tail directions and lengths, beak/head identity, eye size, plumage, belly contour, charcoal color, canvas and transparency. Whole coherent bird drawings, no separate parts, no captions or background.
packing: cwebp lossless -exact -z 9; decoded RGBA verified identical
runtimeCorrection: Canonical walk0 beak core traced relative to the measured eye; forehead and throat blend into each complete pose. Only horizontal left-facing flight, braking, landing, settle, neutral and walk poses use this correction.
